It really is. It's the only distro I've tried yet where Steam just worked. (Sorry RMS, but while I like free software, in the meaning you use it in, I'm not a zealot)

The interface is also really easy to use. There's been very very few cases where I had to turn to a search engine to figure out how to do something. Last two cases I can recall were trying to pin programs to the quicklaunch area of the panel, and trying to add custom right click options to nemo.

I freely admit the taskbar pinning is easier in Windows (8.1 in my dual boot case) and that right click to run as administrator is a function Nemo needs to have. However, my Nemo now has a right click run with sudo option, so that's one down, and I can add further custom actions quite easily now that I've figured it out.

I'm thinking that right click sorting of my Downloads folder into ~/Videos, ~/Pictures, ~/Books, etc... would be a nice feature to have, and I'm pretty sure it won't be hard. Most of it would just be by file extension or MIME type.

Just wanted to add a blanket endorsement of Linux mint Debian edition. Specifically the mate version. It is probably the greatest OS I have ever used. Incredibly stable, efficient, easy, and powerful. Highly recommended. And so far, still no bullshit systemd.
